newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MARKET CHEERS POSSIBLE RANDGOLD MINE MERGE.
newsitem.headline: MARKET CHEERS POSSIBLE RANDGOLD MINE MERGE.

text.p: Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd may be looking to combine three of its mines and this pleased the market, analysts said on Friday after the group cautioned shareholders certain proposals were being considered.
"Shareholders of Durban Deep, Buffels and Blyvoor... are advised that proposals are under consideration which could have a material effect on the price of shares," the mines said earlier.
Shares in Randgold's Durban Roodepoort Deep Ltd , Buffelsfontein Gold Mines Ltd and Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd rose on the announcement.

"I would say that they are looking to bring those companies together as a single entity. Probably looking at the feasibility to see if these companies would benefit from being combined," said Angus Auchterlonie, analyst at Mathison and Hollidge Inc.
"The market thinks it would be a good thing," he added.
No further details were given in the brief announcement and mine managers Randgold could not be reached for comment.
By 1230 GMT Buffelsfontein shares jumped to 19 rand each from 18 rand, Blyvooruitzicht rose to 520 cents from 500 cents and Durban Deep moved up to 31.25 rand from 30.50 rand.

Analysts said that merging these mines -- in whatever form, be it a complete merger or shared synergies -- was in line with Randgold's philosophy of rationalising mining areas and creating economies of scale.
Should these mines merge, they follow in the footsteps of Randgold's Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd and its Grootvlei Proprietary Mines Ltd .
Harmony is bidding for Grootvlei and on Friday provided the details of the scheme under which it would acquire it.

Harmony will issue some 3.10 million shares for the cancellation of issued Grootvlei shares not held by Harmony. Grootvlei shareholders registered, most likely, on June 6 will receive 30 Harmony shares for every 100 Grootvlei shares held.
When the scheme becomes operative, Grootvlei will become a wholly-owned subsidary of Harmony and its listings on the Johannesburg and London Stock Exchanges will be terminated.
The new company is likely to go one step further. In February Harmony announced it planned to bid for Consolidated Modderfontein Mines Ltd which neighbours Grootvlei.
On Friday Harmony shares added 50 cents to 33.00 rand.
"Randgold is taking South African mining away from the old-fashioned seperate mines, separate listings business," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Analysts said that many mining operations were quite aged and this made analysis and forecasting difficult. The stock market's positive reaction to the announcements indicated that they saw benefits from Randgold's plans, they added.

"Randgold are going in with a fairly entrepreneurial, aggressive approach. The market is giving them the benefit of the doubt based on their other successes. The market is giving them credit for innovation," another analyst said.

While this year's first quarter results are only due next week, Blyvooruitzicht has shown a steady increase in quarterly profits since acquired from Gengold in November 1995, along with other mines termed marginal.
In the December quarter it made 18.81 million rand from 11.40 million in the preceding quarter.
Buffelsfontein, also sold to Randgold by Gengold, held December quarter profit fairly steady at 23.88 million rand.
